peerMapping.justification: The block keeps NATGAS as target and uses CL as the single primary_index_hedge despite the legacy field name. Peer weights are positive and sum to exactly 1.00. BRENTOIL receives 0.40 for closest listed comparability after the CL hedge and 36.44 USD millions of displayed 24-hour perp liquidity. BE receives 0.25 because the gas input-cost and power-generation link is strong even with only 1.355 USD millions. COPPER receives 0.20 as a cyclical industrial-demand and risk-on proxy with 6.262 USD millions. SP500 receives only 0.15 because it is highly liquid at 50.729 USD millions but supplies a generic macro channel rather than a natural-gas-specific exposure.

peers.name: Brent crude oil
peers.reason: Brent crude oil is the global seaborne energy benchmark; oil-linked LNG contracts, fuel switching in power and industry, and common growth, inflation and US-dollar shocks make its returns economically comparable to natural gas, and its displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is 36.44 USD millions.

peers.name: Copper
peers.reason: Copper is an industrial-growth and electrification proxy: construction, manufacturing, grid investment and data-center power demand tie it to the same macro demand and inflation and US-dollar cycle that moves natural gas, with displayed 24-hour perp liquidity of 6.262 USD millions.

peers.name: Bloom Energy
peers.reason: Bloom Energy sells fuel-cell power systems whose economics are tied to natural gas or biogas input costs and to power-market demand; this direct input-cost and power-demand link earns weight even though displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is only 1.355 USD millions.

peers.name: S&P 500
peers.reason: SP500 is the broad risk-on proxy: stronger equities usually imply better industrial demand, power load, and capital availability for energy supply, while risk-off selloffs often coincide with demand downgrades. Its 50.729 USD millions liquidity is very high, so the weight is capped for lower gas specificity.

primary_index_hedge.name: WTI crude oil
primary_index_hedge.reason: WTI crude is the most liquid listed energy-complex hedge available in CORE_UNIVERSE, with 40.091 USD millions of displayed 24-hour perp liquidity versus NATGAS at 2.186 USD millions; it shares fuel-demand, inventory, and broad energy shock sensitivity with natural gas while leaving weather and storage idiosyncrasy unhedged.

peerMapping.historyMethod: daily-rebalanced peer spot total returns using the fixed Kimi weights; unavailable pre-listing peers are omitted and remaining weights renormalized once at least three peers exist; the browser rebases the basket to the target spot level at the first shared date of each selected chart range

liveSplice.method: current TradeXYZ perp mid divided by that peer's TradeXYZ close on its latest spot date; available Kimi weights renormalized and applied as a one-period return from the published peer spot endpoint; USD cash close is retained for disclosure but never mixed with a differently scaled perp contract

underlierSelection.method: highest summed live contract volume; open interest and contract count break ties

model.name: ATM-straddle-implied lognormal distribution
model.description: Each target uses the nearest paired liquid ATM call and put. Their combined ask implies the expiration distribution shown on the chart.
model.measure: option-implied, not a historical or physical forecast
